title: Tewantin National Park, Wooroi

bikeon.heading: Tewantin National Park, Wooroi
paras: Tewantin National Park protects rainforest, open eucalypt forest and the last wallum remnants between Noosa and Cooroy, on the traditional Country of the Kabi Kabi people. Much of it was once State Forest 959. After years of lobbying by the Noosa Parks Association the forest was declared national park in 2010, and land from the Yurol and Ringtail state forests was added from 2011. Its forestry past lingers: a heritage site along Gyndier Drive holds remains of an old forestry camp, including references to Chinese workers. The Wooroi day-use area, shaded by coastal she-oaks and bloodwoods, is a historic picnic spot and the trailhead for eleven mountain bike trails, from the easy Hovea loop to the one way Turn 10, managed by Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service with the Noosa Trailblazers Mountain Bike Club. Listen for eastern whipbirds, and watch for swamp wallabies, echidnas and glossy black cockatoos.

story: You're riding through Tewantin National Park. This section of the park is known as the Wooroi section, named after the historic Wooroi picnic ground, today the day use area and the trailhead for eleven mountain bike trails.
The park protects rainforest, open eucalypt forest and the last patches of wallum heath between Noosa and Cooroy, on the Country of the Kabi Kabi people.

Most of it was state forest until 2010, when years of lobbying by the Noosa Parks Association saw it declared a national park, and land from the Yurol and Ringtail forests has been added since. Along Gyndier Drive, a heritage site still holds traces of an old forestry camp.

The trails are managed by the Queensland Parks and Wildlife Service with the Noosa Trailblazers Mountain Bike Club. Listen for whipbirds, and watch for swamp wallabies, echidnas and glossy black cockatoos.
